clue.text: Manchester City's new rig — topping !

indicators.note: a new rig is a fresh fitting-out, and rigging also means fiddling, so the club's name is rearranged

parts.note: the football club's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A football club's new kit is declared absolutely splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new rig' looks like the team's new strip, but it tells you to rearrange MANCHESTER CITY; 'topping' is not praise but a dessert covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic cream is an artificial whipped product spread over desserts as a topping.

clue.text: Some Americans look for rejection, on taking flight

indicators.note: fleeing means turning tail, so the words before are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to look for is to seek
nay is a word of refusal

explanation.surface: Someone searching for a refusal just as a plane departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on taking flight' turns the whole run SEEKNAY back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name for people from the United States, so they are some Americans.

clue.text: Heather follows stratagem of dribbling

indicators.note: the heather word comes after the stratagem word, giving the order of the two pieces

parts.note: a stratagem is a trick
ling is a name for common heather

explanation.surface: A plant name comes after a ploy used by a footballer running with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickling and dribbling both describe a liquid flowing in a thin, slow stream.

clue.text: Suet roly-poly acceptable for those off to train here?

definitions.text: for those off to train here

indicators.note: a roly-poly is a rolled pudding, and rolling the letters about mixes them up

parts.note: on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable

explanation.surface: Asking whether a suet pudding is fit food for people catching a train.
explanation.walkthrough: Suet roly-poly is a British steamed pudding; here 'roly-poly' rearranges SUET into EUST. EUSTON is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a London mainline station where travellers board trains heading north.

clue.text: Persisted in maintaining a sort of tidiness

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variety of it, so the following word is reworked into another form

explanation.surface: Someone kept up a kind of neatness doggedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' tells you to rearrange the letters of TIDINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To have insisted is to have stuck firmly to a claim, persisting in upholding it.

clue.text: Blushing when in company, I believe

indicators.note: the colour word goes inside the company abbreviation, so the second is a container

parts.note: blushing is going red

explanation.surface: Someone admits to blushing in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I believe' looks like a speaker's aside but is the definition: a credo is a creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Credo is Latin for this phrase and names a statement of belief, a creed.

clue.text: Knotted tie, lent to confer rank

indicators.note: a knotted thing is twisted and tangled, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tie tied in a knot is borrowed to give someone status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knotted' mixes up the letters of TIE and LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them a title, bestowing a rank or style.

clue.text: Instead of this savoury one has ice-cream?

indicators.note: the phrase is offered in place of the dish, its letters standing for those of the dish in another order

explanation.surface: Someone orders ice-cream rather than the savoury course.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE HAS ICE-CREAM, rearranged, spell the savoury dish; 'Instead of' signals that one stands for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a baked pasta dish in cheese sauce, a classic savoury course.

clue.text: Make a speech at the dance and prepare to drive off?

definitions.text: Make a speech at the dance

explanation.surface: An orator at a ball who is also a golfer about to tee off.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, to address the ball is to take up the stance before striking it from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking to the guests at a formal dance, or settling into position before a golf drive.

clue.text: Blades desperate character declines to use

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strong-man cartoon character from the British comic The Dandy
to decline in the sense of fade away is to die

explanation.surface: A desperate man turns down the chance to use knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blades' is an old word for dashing young men about town, not knives. Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades and dandies are both old terms for fashionable, showy young men.

clue.text: P.C. cites disorderly Thomas

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters as printed, a police constable

explanation.surface: A police officer reports a man named Thomas for disorderly conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thomas' recalls Doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe without proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting Thomas is the type of the disbeliever, so a Thomas is a doubter.

clue.text: Used by sailors to secure birds perched on rocks?

indicators.note: the birds sit on the rocks, so the bird word follows the rocks word

parts.note: a reef is a ridge of rocks in the sea
knots are small wading birds

explanation.surface: Seabirds sit on rocks that sailors know well.
explanation.walkthrough: The knot is a sandpiper, so 'birds' gives KNOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Reef knots are the square knots sailors tie to secure sails and lines.

clue.text: Smelly oil causing rodent to recoil

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the words before are read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A foul-smelling oil makes a rat shrink back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoil' turns RAT TO back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottar, also attar, is a fragrant oil pressed from rose petals; 'smelly' here means scented.

clue.text: Is returning to hide to see bird

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to a birdwatching hide to spot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like the birdwatcher's shelter, but it is an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Deny a fee, outrageously, to these Arab fighters?

indicators.note: acting outrageously means behaving wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Refusing payment, outrageously, to some guerrillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' rearranges DENY A FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fedayeen are Arab guerrilla fighters, particularly Palestinian commandos.

clue.text: Lido alarm! This animal on the loose!

indicators.note: something on the loose runs free, so the letters are let out of order

explanation.surface: Panic at an open-air pool because an animal has escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the loose' rearranges LIDO ALARM. A lido is a British public open-air swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Amended map with event's route for walkers

indicators.note: an amended text is altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A revised map shows the course of an organised walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amended' rearranges MAP and EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavement is the paved strip beside a road on which pedestrians walk.

clue.text: Travel in it, and see gnat swarm circling round swamp

indicators.note: the jumbled gnat letters ring round the rest, making a container
gnats in a swarm move about in disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a bog is a swamp

explanation.surface: A swarm of gnats circles over a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swarm' mixes up GNAT into T...GAN, which 'circling' wraps round O and BOG; 'Travel in it' is the definition, the sledge you ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sledge, a vehicle you ride in down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Second-rate nut-oil product — it's toxic

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate

indicators.note: a product is something made, so the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: An inferior nut oil turns out to be poisonous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' rearranges NUT-OIL to OTULIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Botulin is the bacterial poison behind botulism, a deadly toxin.

clue.text: A nauseating upbringing

parts.note: an upbringing here is a thing that brings food up, a sickening agent rather than a childhood

explanation.surface: A miserable childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Fabric that appears tawdry stuff, draped over nude

indicators.note: the cheap stuff is hung around the bare word, so it is a container

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods
nude means bare

explanation.surface: A cheap-looking cloth thrown over a naked figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draped over' says the cheap stuff hangs round the nude, so BARE goes inside TAT; 'that appears' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a striped upholstery cloth of silk with satin stripes.

clue.text: Feast fit for a king, note!

parts.note: regal means royal, fit for a king
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A banquet worthy of a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feast' is a verb here, to entertain lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to feast them with lavish food and drink.

clue.text: Plays his part although not a hit

definitions.text: Plays his part although not a hit

parts.words: Plays his part although not a hit
parts.note: a film walk-on plays a role without being a star, and in cricket some runs come without a hit off the bat

explanation.surface: An actor does his bit though the show flops.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs such as byes and wides scored without the bat touching the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film walk-on performer, and also a cricket run conceded without a stroke.

clue.text: A third party insurance launched as a defence

parts.note: the Liberals were Britain's third party, LIB for short

indicators.note: something launched is just starting, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Buying third-party cover to protect yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third party' looks like insurance jargon, but it is the Liberal party; 'launched' takes the first letter of 'insurance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that one was elsewhere, used as a defence against a charge.

clue.text: Being in this state enabled me to get changed

definitions.text: Being in this state enabled me to get changed

indicators.note: getting changed means being altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says their condition allowed them to change clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get changed' rearranges ENABLED ME, and the whole clue also describes the answer: what is open to correction can be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Emendable means open to correction, capable of being changed.

clue.text: Team ill-prepared for unsurpassed achievement

indicators.note: prepared here means made ready in a new form, so the letters before it are worked into another order

explanation.surface: A badly prepared side aims for a record performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-prepared' reads as one word about a weak side, but 'ill' is fodder and 'prepared' rearranges TEAM ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record is the best ever, never bettered.

clue.text: Entices, using every cunning ruse

parts.note: all means every

indicators.note: cunning means devious, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: Someone lures people in with every crafty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' rearranges RUSE to URES.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to tempt or attract, as to entice is.

clue.text: Lanky and too thin, perhaps it may be said about the age

definitions.text: Lanky and too thin, perhaps it may be said about the age

parts.words: Lanky and too thin, perhaps it may be said about the age
parts.note: teeth that look long and thin, with gums receding, are a sign of growing old

explanation.surface: A tall, skinny person is described as getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from horses, whose gums recede with age so their teeth look longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Long in the tooth is an idiom for old, getting on in years.
